thread.title: Qualcomm-Broadcom Talks Productive But Still Unfruitful

author: thestreet.com
title: Qualcomm-Broadcom Talks Productive But Still Unfruitful
text:
Qualcomm Inc. ( QCOM ) again rebuked Broadcom Ltd. ( AVGO ) in a Friday statement, but said talks with the hostile suitor were "constructive."
The chipmakers met Wednesday to discuss Broadcom's sweetened $82 per share bid. Qualcomm said that the offer, which Broadcom raised from $70 per share earlier in February, undervalues the company and carries "unacceptably high" regulatory risk.
Shares of Qualcomm dropped 0.1% to $65.20 before the open on Friday. Broadcom gained 0.5% to $252.97.
The companies have been at odds since Broadcom CEO Hock Tan launched the hostile bid in November. Broadcom's offer values Qualcomm's equity at more than $120 billion, and would be the largest tech deal ever. Broadcom said Monday that it has raised $100 billion from a dozen banks and a private equity consortium including Silver Lake LP, KKR & Co. ( KKR ) and CVC Capital Partners Ltd.
While the revised bid is still problematic, Qualcomm said, Broadcom agreed to consider greater divestitures to reduce regulatory risk. Broadcom previously said it would sell Qualcomm's WiFi processors that go into wireless local area networks and its radio frequency front-end chips to ease regulatory passage.
However, Qualcomm said Broadcom resisted other regulatory concessions.
Qualcomm's licensing business is a sensitive issue. The wireless IP licensing operation has battled with Apple Inc. (AAPL) and regulatory bodies in the U.S. and overseas.
"Broadcom also declined to respond to any questions about its intentions for the future of Qualcomm's licensing business, which makes it very difficult to predict the antitrust-related remedies that might be required," Qualcomm said Friday. Moreover, Broadcom demanded to control "all material decisions" about the IP business in between a deal signing and closing.
Broadcom CEO Hock Tan is not a fan of the business. "We will reset the business model so it is not a contentious issue," Tan said in a Feb. 12 interview with CNBC, suggesting that fines from regulators have exceeded profits over the last three quarters. "That's not a sustainable model. We have to change it. It's broken."
The companies have until Qualcomm's March 6 shareholder meeting to talk through their differences. Broadcom is challenging Qualcomm's nominees at the meeting, but dialed down the hostility on Tuesday when it said it would nominate just six directors rather than 11.
